personas.name: two-week-wait-suspected-malignancy-skin-punch-complete
personas.description: Well-formed dermatology referral: a suspicious pigmented lesion, punch biopsy of skin requested (first-line), no bleeding-risk factors, every completeness field present — the suspected-malignancy indication itself meets NICE NG12 two-week-wait eligibility and escalates triage regardless of the requested urgency — expect usually-appropriate + low bleeding risk + two-week-wait + accept.

indication.clinicalQuestion: Irregular pigmented lesion on the back, ABCDE features positive, growing over 3 months — exclude melanoma.
indication.relevantHistory: Fair skin, history of childhood sunburns. No previous skin cancer.

lesion.lesionDescription: 8mm irregular pigmented macule, asymmetric borders, variable colour, left upper back.

triage.notes: Dermoscopy already performed in clinic, images attached.

expected.anticoagulantAction: Low bleeding risk: proceed without specific anticoagulant action; standard haemostasis precautions.

personas.name: two-week-wait-cancer-staging-liver-core-needle-anticoagulant-high-risk
personas.description: Known lymphoma requiring liver biopsy for staging: core-needle liver biopsy is first-line, cancer-staging also meets two-week-wait eligibility, but the patient is on warfarin — a high periprocedural bleeding risk overrides an otherwise appropriate, complete request and the recommendation is to query the referrer (anticoagulation must be addressed before proceeding) — expect usually-appropriate + high bleeding risk + two-week-wait + query-referrer.

indication.clinicalQuestion: PET-avid liver lesion on staging scan for newly diagnosed follicular lymphoma — confirm hepatic involvement before starting treatment.
indication.relevantHistory: Newly diagnosed follicular lymphoma. Atrial fibrillation on warfarin, target INR 2.0-3.0.

triage.notes: Oncology requests bridging anticoagulation plan before the biopsy slot is confirmed.

expected.anticoagulantAction: High bleeding risk: withhold the anticoagulant (Warfarin) per BSG / ESGE timing and consider bridging; correct the INR to < 1.5.

Patient on an anticoagulant — high periprocedural bleeding risk.
A "cancer-staging" indication meets NICE NG12 two-week-wait eligibility.

flags.suggestedAction: Book on a suspected-cancer two-week-wait pathway; complete within 14 days.

personas.name: characterise-lesion-thyroid-fna-borderline-platelets-incomplete
personas.description: Fine-needle aspiration of an indeterminate thyroid nodule found incidentally: FNA of thyroid is first-line to characterise the lesion, borderline thrombocytopenia gives a moderate (not high) bleeding-risk band — which alone does not block acceptance — and a few administrative fields were left blank on the referral form — expect usually-appropriate + moderate bleeding risk + routine + accept, completeness below 100.

indication.relevantHistory: Nodule found incidentally on a CT scan for an unrelated reason. No compressive symptoms. Mild chronic liver disease with borderline platelet count.

lesion.lesionDescription: 1.4cm left thyroid nodule, solid, mildly hypoechoic on ultrasound.

triage.notes: Patient counselled on incidental finding; not anxious to be seen urgently.

expected.anticoagulantAction: Moderate bleeding risk: confirm a recent platelet count and clotting screen.

firedRules.description: A thyroid biopsy is a recommended target for "characterise-lesion".
No cancer-pathway escalation; triage follows the requested urgency (routine).

flags.suggestedAction: Confirm a recent platelet count; consider transfusion for higher-risk sites.
Query the referrer for the specific question the biopsy should answer.
